The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. The root cause was confirmed: in sqlparse/sql.py, TokenList.insert_before had an inverted isinstance check (`if isinstance(where, int)` instead of `if not isinstance(where, int)`), causing it to call self.token_index(where) on plain integers (passing an int as the token to find via list.index, raising "ValueError: X is not in list") while skipping the conversion for actual Token objects (passing a Token object as a list index, which would TypeError). This matches the reported "ValueError: 4 is not in list" and explains broad regression since insert_before is used in formatting/reindent code paths and SQL injection-prevention/CLI-level tests that format SQL. I already fixed this by swapping the condition to match the correct pattern used in insert_after. Now running smoke tests to confirm formatting works end-to-end (reindent filter uses insert_before internally through other mechanisms, and general parsing/grouping also exercises token_index via group_tokens).
